newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Swedish shares close higher buoyed by firmer debt.
newsitem.headline: Swedish shares close higher buoyed by firmer debt.

text.p: Sweden's sharemarket closed with gains on Monday, buoyed by firmer debt markets.
The Stockholm general index rose 1.04 percent to 2,285.91 after shares worth 3.60 billion crowns changed owners.
The index received a last minute boost with big buying in telecoms giant Ericsson and building company Skanska.
Ericsson closed 5.5 crowns higher at 200 crowns.
Skanska earlier in the day announced that it was to create a new company with IKANO, owned by the family which founded furniture retailer IKEA, that would specialise in factory outlet stores.
It closed 13 crowns higher at 292.5 crowns, dragging the building sector index up 2.57 percent, the day's best performing sector.
Drugs major Astra closed one higher at 329 crowns after holding a presentation day in London.
Forestry companies also posted good gains and the sector index rose 1.59 percent. MoDo climbed six to 190 crowns while SCA closed was 4.5 higher at 141.5 crowns.
Brokers said the focus on Tuesday would be the central bank's inflation report and a widely expected cut in key interest rate, the repo.
